questions.q: When did the Strata Property Act replace the Condominium Act?
questions.explain: July 1, 2000. The Standard Bylaws applied to every strata from January 1, 2002.
questions.ref: Lesson 11 · The strata concept and unit entitlement

questions.q: What does a strata lot's unit entitlement determine?
choices: Only its annual property tax assessment
Its share of common property and expenses
The number of seats it holds on council
The maximum price it can be resold for
questions.explain: It sets each lot's share of ownership of common property and of the strata's expenses (Form V).
questions.ref: Lesson 11 · The strata concept and unit entitlement

questions.q: Total unit entitlement is 8,000; a lot has 64. What is its share of a $200,000 special levy?
questions.ref: Lesson 11 · The strata concept and unit entitlement

questions.q: How is unit entitlement usually calculated for residential strata lots?
questions.explain: Habitable area, which excludes patios, balconies, garages, parking and storage (other than closets).
questions.ref: Lesson 11 · The strata concept and unit entitlement

questions.q: What vote is needed to allocate strata expenses on a basis other than unit entitlement?
choices: A ¾ vote of the owners
questions.explain: A unanimous resolution, registered at the land title office.
questions.ref: Lesson 11 · The strata concept and unit entitlement

questions.q: Who owns the common property in a strata development?
choices: The owners, as tenants in common
questions.explain: Owners hold it as tenants in common (by unit entitlement); the strata corporation controls and maintains it.
questions.ref: Lesson 11 · Common property and who gets to use it

questions.q: How does limited common property differ from a short term exclusive use permission?
choices: LCP is personal; a permission runs with the lot
LCP runs with the lot; a permission is personal
Both last a maximum of one year
Only LCP can be cancelled at any time
questions.explain: LCP attaches to the strata lot; short term exclusive use is a personal, cancellable privilege.
questions.ref: Lesson 11 · Common property and who gets to use it

questions.q: What vote can designate common property as LCP without amending the strata plan?
choices: A majority vote at a council meeting
A ¾ vote at a general meeting, then filing
A unanimous vote of all the owners
An 80% vote of owners and a court order
questions.explain: A ¾ resolution filed at the LTO (recorded in the Common Property Record). Amending the plan itself needs a unanimous vote.
questions.ref: Lesson 11 · Common property and who gets to use it

questions.q: What's the maximum term of a short term exclusive use permission for an ordinary storage locker?
questions.explain: One year (renewable). Up to 5 years for a parking stall with owner-installed EV charging.
questions.ref: Lesson 11 · Common property and who gets to use it

questions.q: Which arrangement is no longer allowed for parking stalls in new residential strata plans?
choices: Stalls forming part of a strata lot
questions.explain: Separate-lot stalls appear only in some older residential plans.
questions.ref: Lesson 11 · Parking stalls and storage lockers

questions.q: How long does a strata have to decide an owner's request to install EV charging?
questions.explain: Three months, and it can't unreasonably refuse (though it can set reasonable conditions).

questions.q: A significant change to common property for EV charging needs what vote?
questions.explain: EV-related approvals that would normally need ¾ drop to a majority.

questions.q: When is a strata corporation created?
choices: At the first annual general meeting
When the strata plan is deposited
When half the lots are sold
questions.explain: On deposit of the strata plan at the land title office (s.2).

questions.q: A court awards $500,000 against a strata corporation. Who ultimately pays?
questions.explain: A judgment against the strata is a judgment against all owners, shared by unit entitlement (except an owner who sued).

questions.q: Why might a mixed-use strata create sections?
choices: So each group bears its own costs
questions.explain: Sections let groups (e.g. commercial and residential) handle and pay for matters affecting only their own lots.

questions.q: Which is NOT normally covered by the strata corporation's insurance?
questions.explain: Owners need their own coverage for contents, deductibles passed on to them, and gaps that lead to special levies.

questions.q: How long does a strata have to provide copies of its bylaws and rules on request?
questions.explain: One week for bylaws and rules; two weeks for other records.
questions.ref: Lesson 11 · Records and who can see them

questions.q: A tenant has a 4-year lease of a residential strata lot. What rights do they get?
choices: None, since only owners have strata rights
The landlord's powers, after written notice
Only the right to vote on annual budgets
Full ownership rights over the strata lot
questions.explain: s.148: tenants on leases of 3 years or more are assigned the landlord's powers and duties, once they give the strata written notice.
questions.ref: Lesson 11 · Records and who can see them

questions.q: What is the maximum a strata can charge for an Information Certificate (Form B)?
questions.explain: $35 plus up to 25 cents per page for copies, delivered within 8 days.
questions.ref: Lesson 11 · What the buyer can get, and what you must read

questions.q: Which document must be attached to a Form B?
questions.explain: Rules, current budget and the most recent depreciation report (and any electrical planning report).
questions.ref: Lesson 11 · What the buyer can get, and what you must read

questions.q: What is a Certificate of Payment (Form F) mainly used for?
choices: Showing the monthly strata fee amount
Allowing a transfer to be registered
questions.explain: The LTO won't register a transfer of a strata lot without one (except court-ordered sales). It's valid for 60 days.
questions.ref: Lesson 11 · What the buyer can get, and what you must read

questions.q: How long is a Certificate of Payment valid once issued?
questions.explain: 60 days. The buyer's lawyer or notary usually orders it shortly before completion.
questions.ref: Lesson 11 · What the buyer can get, and what you must read

questions.q: Why did the buyer's claim fail in Sask v. Brooke?
choices: The seller had no duty to disclose
The minutes showed the leak history
The special levy was too small
The strata never had any leaks
questions.explain: The buyer had the minutes, which described the leaks, so she couldn't show reasonable reliance on the seller's false statement.
questions.ref: Lesson 11 · What the buyer can get, and what you must read

questions.q: How far back should licensees review strata minutes, where available?
questions.explain: At least the preceding two years of council, general and section meeting minutes.
questions.ref: Lesson 11 · What the buyer can get, and what you must read

questions.q: What standard must a strata council member meet?
choices: The standard of a professional engineer
Only a duty to avoid committing fraud
No legal standard applies to volunteers
questions.explain: s.31: honesty and good faith, and the care, diligence and skill of a reasonably prudent person.

questions.q: When must a developer call the first AGM?
choices: Within 1 year of filing the strata plan
Within 6 weeks of 50%+1 sold or 9 months
Only once all of the lots have been sold
Whenever a group of owners requests it
questions.explain: Within 6 weeks after the earlier of 50% + 1 of the lots being conveyed or 9 months after the first conveyance.
questions.ref: Lesson 11 · The developer's first council and the handover

questions.q: How much written notice is required for a strata general meeting?
questions.explain: At least 20 days' written notice.

questions.q: What share of votes can demand a special general meeting?
questions.explain: Owners holding at least 20% of the votes can demand an SGM in writing.

questions.q: When can a mortgagee vote in place of a strata owner?
choices: Whenever the owner misses a mortgage payment
On security-related matters, with 3 days' notice
On any matter at all, if the owner agrees
Never, because only owners can ever vote
questions.explain: Only if the mortgage gives the right, with at least 3 days' written notice, on insurance, maintenance, finance or matters affecting its security.

questions.q: Two co-owners of a strata lot can't agree how to vote. What happens?
choices: They each get half a vote
questions.explain: If co-owners can't agree, the chair must not count their vote on that matter.

questions.q: Whom does a strata property manager represent?
questions.explain: The strata corporation. The manager takes instructions only from council and owes it fiduciary duties.

questions.q: Which expense would normally come from the contingency reserve fund?
questions.explain: The CRF covers expenses that occur less often than once a year.

questions.q: What's the minimum annual contribution to the CRF?
questions.explain: At least 10% of the operating fund budget, considering the latest depreciation report.

questions.q: A selling owner asks for a refund of their CRF contributions. What's the answer?
choices: Yes, if a ¾ vote approves
Only if the CRF is overfunded
questions.explain: s.101 expressly prohibits returning CRF contributions.

questions.q: If the bylaws are silent, how much can council spend from the operating fund without approval?
choices: Up to $5,000 in any one year
Up to 10% of the annual operating budget
Nothing at all without a ¾ vote
questions.explain: The lesser of 5% of the year's operating contributions or $2,000 (plus emergency spending).

questions.q: The developer's interim budget underestimated expenses by 15%. What's the consequence?
choices: The developer pays it plus a penalty
Nothing, since it was only an estimate
The first AGM must be postponed
questions.explain: The developer pays the shortfall; over 10%, it also pays a penalty of double (or triple) the shortfall.

questions.q: A developer conveys the first lot 8 months after depositing the plan. Interim operating expenses are $200,000. What must it pay into the CRF?
questions.explain: Within the first year: 10% of estimated operating expenses = $20,000.

questions.q: What vote is needed for a special levy shared by unit entitlement?
questions.explain: ¾ by unit entitlement; unanimous for any other sharing method.

questions.q: A ¾ vote fails for a levy to fix a dangerous balcony. What can the strata do?
choices: Nothing until the next annual general meeting
Pass it by majority, then seek court approval
Charge the levy anyway, as an emergency
Let council impose it without any vote
questions.explain: s.173(2): for repairs necessary for safety or to prevent significant loss, a majority plus a Supreme Court application within 90 days.

questions.q: A levy instalment falls due after completion of a sale. Under s.109, who pays it?
choices: The seller, as the former owner
The buyer, as the new owner
questions.explain: Whoever owns the lot when the payment is due pays it, unless the contract shifts it.

questions.q: Which wording should a special levy holdback clause use?
questions.explain: Match s.108: "approved" rather than "passed", and "special levy" rather than "assessment".

questions.q: How often must a strata obtain a depreciation report after its first one?
questions.explain: Every 5 years. Stratas with fewer than 5 lots are exempt.
questions.ref: Lesson 11 · Depreciation reports and electrical planning reports

questions.q: Over what period does a depreciation report's financial forecast run?
questions.explain: 30 years, showing the effect on the contingency reserve fund.
questions.ref: Lesson 11 · Depreciation reports and electrical planning reports

questions.q: What must a strata do before suing an owner for unpaid fees?
choices: Give at least 2 weeks' written demand
File a lien against the strata lot first
questions.explain: At least two weeks' written notice demanding payment.

questions.q: Can a strata file a lien for unpaid bylaw fines?
choices: Yes, like any other strata debt
No, but it can withhold the Form F
Only after a ¾ vote of owners
questions.explain: No lien for fines or bylaw-remedy costs; the strata can sue or withhold the Certificate of Payment.

questions.q: Which charge ranks ahead of a registered strata lien?
questions.explain: A strata lien beats every other charge except builders liens, Crown liens (not mortgages) and liens for a judgment share.

questions.q: When is an amended bylaw enforceable?
choices: Once it's filed at the LTO
questions.explain: Only once it's filed at the land title office.

questions.q: What can strata rules regulate?
choices: Use of the individual strata lots
Use of common property and assets
Rental of the strata lots to tenants
questions.explain: Rules (made by council) cover common property and common assets, not strata lots.

questions.q: A rule made by council isn't ratified at the next AGM. What happens?
choices: It needs filing at the LTO
questions.explain: Unratified rules lapse at the first AGM after they're made.

questions.q: After the second AGM, what vote amends the bylaws of a residential strata?
questions.explain: ¾. Before the second AGM, a residential strata needs a unanimous vote.

questions.q: In a mixed residential and commercial strata, what does a bylaw amendment need after the 2nd AGM?
questions.explain: Both a ¾ vote of residential lots and a ¾ vote of non-residential lots (unless the bylaws say otherwise for non-residential).

questions.q: What must happen before a strata fines an owner?
choices: Written details and a chance to respond
An order from the BC Supreme Court
A ¾ vote at a general meeting first
questions.explain: Complaint, written particulars, a reasonable chance to answer (including a hearing if asked), then a written decision.

questions.q: What is the maximum fine per bylaw contravention under the Regulation (other than short-term rentals)?
questions.explain: $200 per bylaw breach and $50 per rule breach, every 7 days. Short-term rental bylaws: up to $1,000 daily.

questions.q: In Bahmutsky v. Petkau, why did the strata have to pay damages?
choices: It fined a resident too much
It failed to enforce its bylaws
It refused to repair a roof
questions.explain: Enforcing bylaws is mandatory (s.26). The strata threatened a fine for smoking nuisance but never followed through.

questions.q: Since November 24, 2022, what can a strata still restrict?
questions.explain: General rental restrictions are banned; short-term rental restrictions are still allowed.

questions.q: When must a Form K signed by the tenant be given to the strata?
choices: Before the tenant first views the unit
Within 2 weeks of the tenancy starting
Within 30 days of signing the lease
Only at the next annual general meeting
questions.explain: Within two weeks. If the landlord didn't provide the bylaws and Form K, the tenant can end the tenancy within 90 days.

questions.q: Which age-restriction bylaw is allowed today?
questions.explain: Only age restrictions of 55 or older ("not less than 55"). Other ages were removed in 2022.

questions.q: Under the Standard Bylaws, which pet is an owner allowed to keep?
questions.explain: Reasonable numbers of fish and small caged mammals, up to 2 caged birds, and one dog or one cat.

questions.q: Which repair is always the strata's job, even on limited common property?
questions.explain: The strata always repairs structure, exterior, balconies, exterior doors and windows, and fences or railings.

questions.q: What's needed to wind up a strata and sell the whole property?
choices: A ¾ vote of the owners
An 80% vote and a court order
questions.explain: An 80% resolution at a general meeting plus BC Supreme Court approval.
questions.ref: Lesson 11 · Winding up and legal proceedings

questions.q: In Dubas v. Strata Plan VR 92, what vote was needed to hire a brokerage to market the complex?
questions.explain: A majority vote at a general meeting was enough.
questions.ref: Lesson 11 · Winding up and legal proceedings

questions.q: An owner sues the strata and wins. Must they help pay the judgment?
questions.explain: An owner who obtains a judgment against the strata doesn't contribute to it (or to the strata's defence costs).
questions.ref: Lesson 11 · Winding up and legal proceedings

questions.q: What must the minimum term of a ground lease for a leasehold strata be?
questions.explain: At least 50 years.

questions.q: What happens if a leasehold landlord doesn't give notice of non-renewal at least 1 year before expiry?
choices: The tenant must buy the land
questions.explain: The default is an automatic five-year renewal.

questions.q: Does the Home Buyer Rescission Period apply to a leasehold strata purchase?
questions.explain: The HBRP doesn't apply to leasehold interests or homes on leased land.

questions.q: What does a buyer of a leasehold strata lot actually acquire?
choices: Fee simple title to the strata lot itself
An assignment of the strata lot lease
Shares in a non-profit housing cooperative
A revocable licence to occupy the unit
questions.explain: The buyer takes an assignment of the remaining term of the strata lot lease.

questions.q: What does a buyer in a cooperative acquire?
choices: Shares and a lease of a unit
Common property as tenant in common
questions.explain: Shares in the co-op corporation, which entitle them to lease a unit.

questions.q: Why is financing a co-op purchase often harder than a strata purchase?
choices: Co-ops are banned from having mortgages
The buyer has no fee simple to mortgage
Banks never lend on BC co-op purchases
Co-op units can never be resold later
questions.explain: The buyer can offer only a security interest in shares (and maybe a leasehold mortgage).

questions.q: Which statement about selling a co-op interest is correct?
choices: Owners can sell to anyone they choose
The board usually must approve the buyer
The strata council must approve the buyer
Only the original developer can sell
questions.explain: Co-op boards usually approve buyers and have wide discretion.
